title: Differentiate `-c` from `-a packets:`
description:
In TShark's man page, the description for `-a packets:N` implies that
the output file will *contain* N packets, but `-c N` implies only that
tshark will *read* N packets (which further implies the output file
could have fewer packets if `-Y` is used). However, the text also
falsely says the two are equivalent.

This patch causes `-a packets:N` to stop after the output *contains* N
packets when reading from one file to write to another. Fixes #17411.

Some changes were made to dumpcap for clarity with the new variable
names, but the actual behaviour of dumpcap is unchanged; due to the way
it's written, it's significantly more difficult to differentiate packets
seen from packets written.

Closes #17411


Thanks for your work on this @boolean263! Hope this gets in there. Please let me know if there's anything I can help with.

I think that the wording in the documentation is confusing. All the descriptions of `-a packets:count` are the same, and all the descriptions of `-c count` are the same for live data, but one says that it's the same and one says that it's different.

Let's see if I understand the behavior after the patch:

`dumpcap` (including when called by wireshark) has a capture filter with `-f`. `tshark` has a capture filter with `-f` as well as the display filter (`-Y`) and, in two-pass mode (`-2`), the read filter (`-R`).

The display filter also affects what packets are written to a file (as well as any packets that the ones that pass the filter "depend" on, such as parts of reassembles - but note #12597, there are some edge cases where it doesn't work, like when fragmented SCTP packets that are themselves reassembled IP packets, it doesn't go up to another ancestor level when looking for dependent packets. But I digress.)

The `-c` modes all count the number of packets that are "read", where only packets that pass the capture filter and, when `-R` is included in tshark two pass mode, the read filter as well, are considered "read."

The `-a` mode counts packets that are "written," which means that it only counts packets that pass the display filter (or packets that those depend on, see above). Since `dumpcap` doesn't have a display filter / equivalent of `-Y`, for it `-a` and `-c` are the same.

Does that sound right? Obviously that's way too verbose for the documentation.

There's sort of an analogous situation with the tshark `-z` stats after read filters and two-pass mode were relegated to a non-default option. tshark `-z` stats are affected by the `-f` and `-R` filter but not affected by the main `-Y` display filter (but most do have their own private filter).

5409076d (and ff304fe3) reworks the tshark man pages to hopefully be clearer.

New wordings:

> -c <capture packet count>
Set the maximum number of packets to read when capturing live
data.
If reading a capture file, set the maximum number of packets to read.
This includes any packets that do not pass the display filter, so it
may differ from *-a packets:*<capture packet count>.

> -a *packets*_:value
switch to the next file after it contains __value__
packets.
This does not include any packets that do not pass the display filter, so it
may differ from *-c*<capture packet count>.
